subject: NovaCorp evaluation — pricing match and migration schedule
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@novacorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — commercial ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — Alan and I ran the team review this morning. NovaCorp is seriously evaluating Redwood for our inference layer but we have one uphill ask from procurement: the incumbent has offered a 22% effective discount for the first 12 months and a migration credit covering 50% of egress costs for the pilot.

Before we move to legal, procurement wants to understand whether Redwood can:
- match the effective first-year spend (22% equivalent) on a committed package, and
- provide a migration credit (or time-bound egress cap) that reduces our pilot risk, and
- confirm runtime compatibility for our burst workload (we need an interoperability checkpoint with our engineers).

Can you provide a concrete price-match offer and a suggested migration schedule (2–4 week pilot + production ramp) we can share with procurement? Attaching the incumbent quote for reference.

Appreciate a fast turnaround — procurement plans to issue their term sheet by Friday 5/14.

Best,
Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Cloud Procurement, NovaCorp
procurement@novacorp.com

Attachment: incumbent_quote.pdf (referenced)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@novacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — commercial ask

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the incumbent terms.

Short answer: we can match the effective first-year economics with a targeted bundle and provide a limited migration credit tied to pilot KPIs. High-level proposal below:

1) Pricing match (first 12 months)
   - Match ~22% effective discount via a committed 12-month package (consumption + reserved inference capacity).
   - Offer includes a 60% seat/throughput tier uplift for the first 90 days to ensure headroom for burst traffic.

2) Migration credit / egress protection
   - $75k capped migration credit applied to egress and initial integration hours; expires 90 days after pilot start.
   - Alternative: 50% egress cap for pilot (we can implement a blended cap in billing).

3) Technical / interoperability checkpoint
   - We propose a 2-week engineering sync (shared test harness) followed by a 2-week pilot. Karthik will lead the runtime validation.

4) Next steps and timing
   - If procurement confirms budget intent by 5/14, we can lock terms and produce a redlineable term sheet the same day.

I attached a draft pricing workbook and an initial redline to accelerate the legal loop. If this sounds directionally correct, can we schedule a 30-minute procurement + engineering call tomorrow or Wednesday?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachment: Pricing_Workbook_Nova_v1.xlsx, Redline_Novacorp_v1.docx

From: procurement@novacorp.com <procurement@novacorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Choi <alan.choi@novacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — commercial ask

Ben / Karthik,

Thanks for the proposal. A few procurement/legal items we need clarified before moving to signatures:

- Contract term: we prefer a 24-month minimum for committed pricing; will the 22% effective rate still hold if we extend to 24 months?
- Termination / escape: we need an SLA credit schedule and an exit data-export clause (standard for our security team).
- Migration credit conditionality: procurement will require the migration credit to be tied to milestone acceptance (pilot success criteria) and a one-time invoice credit rather than ad-hoc discounts.
- Compliance evidence: please confirm SOC 2 Type II date and provide the last three months of audit log export procedure (we may request a short runbook).

Also, Alan flagged an integration question — our platform uses a bespoke KV cache layer; we need confirmation that Redwood’s runtime can support a nonstandard caching pattern without extensive re-engineering. Karthik, can you have engineering provide a compatibility note we can include in the term sheet?

Procurement timeline: we still plan to circulate an internal term sheet 5/14; if you can provide a redlineable contract and the SOC2 evidence by EOD 5/13 that will keep us on track.

Regards,
NovaCorp Procurement

--

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — commercial ask

Maria / procurement team — thanks for the list. Quick answers and the attachments you requested are included.

- Term length: we can extend the matched effective rate to a 24-month term with a modest taper on the second-year uplift (we maintain 20% effective first-year equivalent when moved to 24 months; workbook shows the breakpoints).
- Exit / SLA: included an SLA credit schedule in the redline (see Redline_Novacorp_v1.docx). Exit export: we’ll provide the export runbook and agree a 30-day export window in section 7.
- Migration credit: we’ll model the credit as a one-time invoice credit tied to pilot acceptance criteria (pilot KPIs defined in Appendix A of the pricing workbook).
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II on 2027-03-10; attached is the compliance summary and the audit-log export runbook (engineering note attached).
- KV cache compatibility: Karthik has prepared a short compatibility note and a proposed lightweight adapter for your KV layer; we can demo this during the engineering sync.

Proposed immediate schedule:
- Thu 5/13 11:00am PT: 30m procurement + legal call to review redline
- Fri 5/14 9:00am PT: engineering sync (Karthik + Alan + Nova eng) to validate KV flow
- Mon 5/17: pilot start (2 weeks) if the above succeed

Please review the attached files and confirm a time for the 5/13 call. If procurement needs the redline in a different format (DocuSign-ready), tell me and I’ll have legal produce it this afternoon.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

—Ben
